key_insight: CEDAR, an evidence-citing and self-auditing LLM pipeline, outperformed trained machine-learning models in predicting pediatric diabetes outcomes, with the largest gains on sparsely screened outcomes.
engineering_relevance: The results support testing evidence-linked, self-auditing LLM pipelines for clinical prediction from heterogeneous records in small-cohort settings.
method: Combine structured records with note-derived social determinants and, for type 1 diabetes, continuous glucose monitoring data.
Use 18 months of follow-up to predict outcomes at 24 months: seven in type 2 diabetes and four in type 1 diabetes.
Generate evidence-citing predictions with self-auditing and assess clinician agreement using the cited evidence and reasoning.
evidence_signal: Across 2,489 youth with type 2 diabetes and 4,018 with type 1 diabetes, pooled AUROC was 0.815 versus 0.656–0.700 and 0.756 versus 0.603–0.631, respectively; only 4 of 70,246 cited values mismatched the chart.
watch_item: External validation and prospective clinical evaluation are needed; citation accuracy and clinician agreement do not establish deployment safety.
paper_title: Agentic LLM reasoning in pediatric diabetes outcome prediction from multimodal medical records
